narrative.overview: NexusAgent is an instrument that is clearly, visibly listening. One luminous control sits at the centre of a quiet, dark console; everything around it exists to show what the agent heard, what it is doing, and how much time is left. The system has one identity and two modes: the expressive widget and the calm operating dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: A single glowing focal control (the round mic) per screen in the widget, always the largest object.
Dark, layered navy grounds with translucent glass panels; four themes (nexus, daylight, emerald, ember) swap only tokens.
Every conversation phase (connecting, idle, listening, transcribing, thinking, speaking, ended, error) has a distinct state, announced in one status line.
Time is visible: the 60 s turn countdown is drawn as an arc around the control (the 120 s session cap is not yet shown).
Dashboard: dense, light, legible; 12 px body text, pill filters, rounded cards.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: In the widget, the signal accent belongs to the agent: the orb, the live dot, the active turn. Decorative surfaces use translucent tints of it (≤ 0.26 alpha lines), never the full colour.

rules.name: The Tenant Owns the Accent Rule
rules.body: Tenant theming flows only through --va-primary* and --nx-accent* variables. Never hard-code a tenant colour into a component.

rules.name: The Quiet Classification Rule
rules.body: The customer never sees how the agent classified them. The accent stays the tenant/theme colour for the whole call (no red or amber mood shift), and no sentiment, complaint, priority, or captured name/phone appears on the customer's screen. That data belongs to the dashboard.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Inside the widget, create hierarchy with weight and tracking first; the widget lives in small iframes and must not grow headings to compete with the orb.

rules.name: The Signal Glow Rule
rules.body: Glow and gradient text are deliberate NexusAgent signature, sanctioned in the widget (the mic orb, live states, the company wordmark). They are not used in the dashboard or on data, numbers or body text.

rules.name: The One Hero Rule
rules.body: The mic is the largest interactive object on every widget screen. Nothing animated or decorative may be larger than it or sit between the status line and it.

dos: Do keep one glowing focal control per widget screen: the mic orb.
Do give every conversation phase a distinct visual state, stated once in the status line.
Do theme through --nx-* and --va-primary* variables so all four themes and tenant colours keep working.
Do keep dashboard numbers in solid colours with the slate text hierarchy.
Do pair status colours with a word or icon.
donts: Don't recolour the widget or show labels, priorities or contact details based on the agent's classification (The Quiet Classification Rule).
Don't use glow or gradient text in the dashboard, on numbers, or on body text (The Signal Glow Rule).
Don't hard-code tenant or theme colours (for example #00E5FF) in components; use the variable.
Don't add a second competing glowing element next to the orb.
Don't grow widget headings to compete with the orb (The Weight-Not-Size Rule).
